title: Comparative efficacy of sedation or analgesia methods for shoulder dislocation
author: Minoru Hayashi
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bzmnp45e

steps.title: Define Study Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria
steps.instruction: Establish the parameters for selecting randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and participants for the review.

substeps.instruction: Include RCTs assessing sedation or analgesia for anterior shoulder dislocation regardless of language or country.
Include published/unpublished articles, conference abstracts, and letters; exclude crossover trials, quasi-experimental studies, and quasi-randomized trials.
Include participants >15 years old with a diagnosis of anterior shoulder dislocation via physical exam or X-ray.

Exclude patients unable to provide informed consent, those with allergies to study medications, multiple trauma, associated humerus fractures (excluding Hill-Sachs and Bankart lesions), hemodynamic instability, or respiratory distress.

steps.title: Define Interventions and Outcomes
steps.instruction: Standardize the interventions to be compared and the primary/secondary outcomes to be measured.

substeps.instruction: Define Intravenous Sedation (IVS): intravenous injection of sedatives (e.g., propofol, etomidate, benzodiazepines, barbiturates, ketamine, dexmedetomidine) with optional analgesics (e.g., opioid, acetaminophen, NSAIDs, pethidine, meperidine).
Define Intra-articular Anesthetic Injection (IAA): injection of local anesthetics (e.g., lidocaine, prilocaine, mepivacaine, ropivacaine, bupivacaine) into the glenohumeral joint.

Define Peripheral Nerve Block (PNB): injection of local anesthetics (e.g., lidocaine, prilocaine, mepivacaine, ropivacaine, bupivacaine) into the brachial plexus (interscalene position) or suprascapular nerve.
Define Placebo or No intervention groups.
Identify Primary Outcomes: Immediate success rate of reduction, patient satisfaction (scale-based interview while awake), and length of hospital stay (minutes).
Identify Secondary Outcomes: All adverse events, pain score (NRS or VAS), time required for reduction (minutes), number of reduction attempts, and total success rate of reduction.

steps.title: Perform Literature Search
steps.instruction: Execute a comprehensive search across electronic databases and other resources to identify eligible studies.

substeps.instruction: Search electronic databases: Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE via PubMed, and EMBASE via Embase.com using specified search strategies.
Search for ongoing or unpublished trials via WHO International Clinical Trials Platform Search Portal (ICTRP) and ClinicalTrials.gov.
Use Google Scholar to find literature citing included studies.
Review reference lists of eligible studies, international guidelines, and articles citing eligible studies.
Contact original authors for unpublished or additional data.

steps.title: Select Studies and Extract Data
steps.instruction: Screen identified literature and extract technical data using a standardized process.

substeps.instruction: Perform independent title and abstract screening by two reviewers (MH and KK).
Perform independent full-text review by the same two reviewers to determine inclusion.
Contact original authors if abstract-only studies have unclear criteria.
Resolve disagreements via discussion or a third reviewer (NK).
Perform independent data extraction using a standardized form pre-checked with 10 randomly selected studies.
Extract information on study design, population, interventions, and outcomes; resolve disagreements via discussion or arbiter (NK).

steps.title: Assess Risk of Bias
steps.instruction: Evaluate the quality of included studies using a standardized tool.

substeps.instruction: Two reviewers (MH and KK) independently assess risk of bias using the Risk of Bias 2 tool.
Resolve disagreements via discussion or a third reviewer (NK).

steps.title: Perform Statistical Analysis
steps.instruction: Pool data and conduct network meta-analysis using R software version 4.0.2 and OpenBUGS.

substeps.instruction: Pool odds ratio, relative risk ratios, and risk difference with 95% CIs for binary variables (immediate and total success rates).
Pool standardized mean differences and 95% CIs for continuous variables (hospital stay, satisfaction, pain score, reduction time, and number of attempts).
Summarize adverse events based on original article definitions without meta-analysis.
Apply intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis for dichotomous data, assuming negative outcomes for dropouts.
For continuous data, perform meta-analysis on available data without imputation per Cochrane handbook.
Calculate missing standard deviations using Altman's method or Cochrane handbook/validated methods if only SE or p-values are provided.
Evaluate heterogeneity using visual inspection of forest plots and the I2 statistic (significant if P < 0.10 via Cochrane Chi2 test).
Assess reporting bias via funnel plots and Egg tests (if ≥10 trials or similar sample sizes).
Conduct network meta-analysis using both fixed-effect and random-effects models; use pairwise meta-analysis or narrative synthesis if network meta-analysis is inappropriate.

steps.title: Conduct Subgroup and Sensitivity Analyses
steps.instruction: Test the robustness of the results through targeted exclusions and subgrouping.

substeps.instruction: Perform subgroup analysis on primary outcomes based on whether the dislocation was first-time or recurrent.
Conduct sensitivity analyses by excluding: non-double blind studies, studies using imputed statistics, studies with high/some concern in ROB, or studies not meeting ideal outcomes.

steps.title: Generate Summary of Findings
steps.instruction: Evaluate the certainty of evidence and produce a final summary table.

substeps.instruction: Two reviewers (MH and NK) evaluate certainty of evidence using Confidence in Network Meta-analysis (CINeMA), with NY as arbiter.
Create a summary of findings table for immediate success rate, patient satisfaction, and length of hospital stay.
